text:
Linda: So I finally got the raised beds finished last weekend, Harold. Four of them, each about eight feet by three.
Harold: Oh, good for you. What did you fill them with?
Linda: A mix of compost, topsoil, and some aged manure from the farm down the road. It smells a bit, but the plants love it.
Harold: Oh, that's the best stuff. What are you planting?
Linda: Tomatoes mostly, three kinds, the big beefsteak ones, some cherry tomatoes, and those, um, heirloom ones, the purple ones. Then peppers, basil, zucchini, and a row of lettuce at the edge.
Harold: Be careful with zucchini. Plant two and you'll have forty. I'm not joking, you will be leaving them on neighbours' porches at night.
Linda: Ha! That's what everybody says. I'm only doing one plant this year.
Harold: Wise. And watch out for slugs on the lettuce. I put crushed eggshells around mine and it helped quite a bit.
Linda: Eggshells, okay. I've also got a problem with the deer. They ate all my hostas last summer.
Harold: Deer are tough. We put up a fence, six feet high, and still one jumped it. Now we have a motion sprinkler. It works pretty well, soaks them, they run off.
Linda: A motion sprinkler, I like that. Where do you get one?
Harold: The garden centre, about thirty dollars. I'll pick one up for you when I go on Saturday.
Linda: Oh, that's so kind. Come for tea afterwards and see the beds.
Harold: Will do. Take care now.
